absent: Locking rules and concurrency protection for capability tables and CPU masks.
Full layouts and numeric values of capability identifiers, MIDR constants and system registers.
Complete state transitions and ordering of capability detection versus CPU hotplug.
Details of Spectre mitigations and cache maintenance trap handlers referenced but not shown.

findings.text: Global table arm64_errata publishes the errata and workaround capabilities known to this build, with each entry carrying a description and capability identity plus matching information; the table ends with an empty terminator.
get_cpu_ops provides read access to the per-CPU operations pointer selected at boot for a given CPU index.
sme_enable_dvmsync records the calling CPU as needing SME DVMSync handling by setting its bit in a global CPU mask.

MIDR matching lists are empty terminated arrays enumerating affected models and revision ranges, with entries conditionally included by build options and evaluated by generic range or multi entry helpers.

Neoverse N1 erratum 1542419 is reported only for Neoverse N1 revisions when the cache type indicates data independent caches, evaluated on the local CPU while non preemptible, with a warning if scope or preemption expectations are violated.

Apple implementation defined PMUv3 is reported only when the kernel runs in hypervisor mode, the sanitised debug feature register reports an implementation defined PMU version, and the MIDR matches a known Apple list covering Icestorm Firestorm Blizzard Avalanche across M1 and M2 families.
Broken GICv3 SEIS is reported only when in hypervisor mode on an Apple MIDR from the same Apple list and when the interrupt virtualisation trap register indicates SEIS.
Enabling the Apple IMPDEF PMU workaround sets one high bit in the hypervisor auxiliary control register without clearing other bits.

SME DVMSync erratum is reported only when the sanitised performance feature register indicates SME and the entry MIDR range matches; its per-CPU enable checks whether the corresponding workaround capability is present on this CPU before recording the CPU.

CPU bring-up method tables are null terminated: device tree boot accepts spin table and PSCI, ACPI boot accepts parking protocol when configured plus PSCI; selected pointers are stored in a per-CPU array sized by maximum CPUs and marked read only after init.
CPU feature logging uses a fixed compile time message prefix defined alongside the feature code.

Capability entries observed use a description, capability number, scope type, match predicate, optional match list or MIDR range or range list, optional fixed revision mask, and optional per-CPU enable callback.

Each erratum follows detect then enable: a match predicate selects affected CPUs or the system, then an optional CPU enable callback applies traps or records state; local errata evaluate per CPU while system features and weak local features allow late CPUs under different rules.

Several lists mark CPUs needing repeated TLB invalidate synchronization, cache maintenance traps, speculative address translation protection, speculative unprivileged load protection, and speculative SSBS handling across Cortex Kryo Neoverse and partner parts.

Trace and counter hazards include TRBE overwrite fill mode, TRBE write out of range, TSB flush failure, broken AMU constant counter, and broken AArch32 AES on specified Cortex Neoverse and Cobalt revisions.

Platform hazards include Cavium ThunderX and OcteonTX2 families, Ampere AC03 and AC04, NVIDIA Carmel CNP and Olympus ordering, Hisilicon CNP, Qualcomm Falkor Kryo and Oryon CNTVOFF, Apple PMU traps and GIC SEIS, and SME DVMSync acknowledgement.
IMPDEF PMU trap enable sets bit 56 of the hypervisor auxiliary control register.
Neoverse N1 1542419 presence depends on the DIC bit of the cache type register at its architected shift.
Revision fix masks observed include bit 8 for Cortex A53 erratum 843419, bit 25 for Cortex A510 r1p1 erratum 2658417, and bit 0 of the revision identifier for C1-Pro r1p2 erratum 4193714.
